options: Multiple Process Pipeline
Massive Parallel Processing
Managed Performance Platform
Master Partition Protocol
Memory Paging Processor
questions.explanation: MPP stands for Massive Parallel Processing, which uses hardware-level concurrency to split one job across multiple nodes.

questions.stem: What is the major difference between concurrent processing and MPP?
options: Concurrent processing depends on developers, whereas MPP depends on hardware
Concurrent processing is only for NoSQL databases, whereas MPP is only for SQL
Concurrent processing is faster in every case than MPP
MPP runs on a single core, whereas concurrent processing needs many
There is no difference; the terms mean the same thing
questions.explanation: There is a major difference: one, concurrent processing, is dependent on the developers and the other, MPP, on hardware.

questions.stem: What does concurrent processing mean in simple words?
options: A single job is split into pieces that run on many nodes
Jobs are queued and run one after another
More than one job runs in parallel, executing some code sets at the same time
A job is paused until hardware becomes available
Code is compiled before it is executed
questions.explanation: Concurrent processing means more than one job runs in parallel and executes some code sets at the same time, usually dependent on the cores handling the queries.

questions.stem: On what does concurrent query capability most often depend?
options: The number of users logged in
The size of the hard disk
The version of the operating system
The cores handling the queries
The colour scheme of the dashboard
questions.explanation: Concurrent processing, where technology can run concurrent queries, is most of the time dependent on the cores handling the queries.

questions.stem: How does MPP execute a single job?
options: It runs the job on one node and caches the result
It waits for all other jobs to finish first
It converts the job into a batch to run overnight
It sends the job to a cloud provider for approval
It divides the job into multiple pieces that run in parallel across multiple nodes
questions.explanation: MPP utilises hardware-level concurrency where one job or code set is divided into multiple pieces and runs in parallel mode across multiple nodes.

questions.stem: Why is a job running under MPP much faster?
options: Because a single job utilises multiple nodes to execute the same code set instead of one node at a time
Because MPP skips validation steps
Because MPP compresses the data before processing
Because MPP only processes a sample of the data
Because MPP runs the job in memory only
questions.explanation: Under MPP a single job utilises multiple nodes to execute the same code set, making it much faster compared with a job using a single node at a time.

questions.stem: What benefit do concurrent and MPP capabilities give a data solution?
options: Lower licensing costs
A huge benefit when it comes to meeting SLAs
Automatic data quality fixes
Elimination of the need for backups
Guaranteed regulatory compliance
questions.explanation: Having concurrent and MPP capability gives a huge benefit to the solution when it comes to meeting SLAs.

questions.stem: In the Big Data era, how are concurrent and MPP capabilities described?
options: As optional luxuries
As obsolete techniques
As a must-have
As relevant only for small datasets
As a security risk
questions.explanation: In the Big Data era, having concurrent and MPP capabilities is described as a MUST-TO-HAVE.

questions.stem: Which statement about MPP is NOT correct?
options: MPP uses hardware-level concurrency
MPP divides one code set into multiple pieces
MPP runs those pieces in parallel across nodes
MPP depends on developers writing many separate jobs
MPP helps a solution meet its SLAs
questions.explanation: MPP depends on hardware, not developers; it is concurrent processing that depends on the developers.

questions.stem: Which scenario is an example of concurrent processing rather than MPP?
options: One large report query split across ten nodes
A single job divided into pieces at the hardware level
A node executing one piece of a larger code set
Hardware partitioning a single query
Several different jobs running in parallel on the available cores at the same time
questions.explanation: Concurrent processing is when more than one job runs in parallel at the same time, whereas MPP splits a single job across multiple nodes.
